chapter: Joining Raeburn and work for other leaders
title: Charts for Tommy Dorsey and Benny Goodman, and Dave Dexter
summary: He tells of charts for Goodman and Dorsey, Benny's puzzlement, Tommy's anger, and manager Jerry Brightman's feud with Dave Dexter.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Let me back up and finish off that first--before we get to Boyd, I want to be sure that we made all the notes here--what did you do for Jimmy and Tommy Dorsey?

It was all conversation. For Tommy I wrote one thing and it was a pop tune of the day and you know I can't remember what came of it. Something happened. I told you about this manager that I had that brought grief to me in various ways, the way Dave Dexter used to insult me in print even though he didn't know me, because he had had this physical fist fight with Jerry and Jerry had beaten him up, so naturally Jerry's clients became his number one pet hate and he would write--
What was Jerry's last name?
Brightman, that was the name he was born with, but he changed it to Herbert J. Morrison.
He would write things like Pete Rugulo's the greatest writer I've heard and he doesn't have to wear a beard to be noticed.
Musical criticisms.
Anyway, we were getting at what?
Your work with Dorsey.
Right.

So I had done this chart for Dorsey, I had done a thing for Benny Goodman and a thing for Dorsey at the same time and Jerry was to deliver my scores and pick up the money, and he brought the thing in to Benny and told me they went through it and Benny looked puzzled but gave him the check. I got a letter from Mel Powell regarding that score about a year later saying that the score--
(Tape went blank for a few seconds)
--there was some fast work with clarinet and piano between Benny and
Mel and Mel indicated in his letter that when he came to those passages Benny would just look at his part instead of playing it, while Mel was playing his part.
He ran through the chart, paid for it; I never heard it, and that was the end of the chart for Benny.
Were the passages difficult for him or just puzzling?
I wouldn't think so. I have no idea.
I thought he could play anything.
I think he can; I don't understand why that happened, but that's what happened, as reported to me.

Now the chart that went to Dorsey, I don't even know whether he ran it down. He paid for it, but he was angry and the reason he was angry was that he had heard that I told people that he offered to make me another Sy Oliver if I would come and write for him, and I didn't do
And that made Sy mad?
It made Tommy mad.
Sy was presumably yelling to Tommy about that, I should imagine?

I really don't know whether it got to Sy. I can't think of why it wouldn't have, but I didn't say anything like that. I'm not the kind of a person that makes snotty remarks about people. I don't do that. But Tommy was upset about that and when I heard that he was upset, I said well, that's life. If he's upset, let him be upset.
